name: Cabo Verde
summary_text: Cabo Verde is workable — Africa's most tolerant jurisdiction alongside South Africa's legal tier. Same-sex relations are legal; employment discrimination based on sexual orientation is prohibited; Praia and Mindelo host visible Pride events; the culture is notably relaxed by regional standards. No explicit GI protections and no LGR statute (administrative practice unclear), but no documented anti-trans violence pattern.

sources.title: Cabo Verde | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations not criminalised in Cabo Verde; employment protections based on sexual orientation (though gender identity/expression/sex characteristics not explicitly referenced); first Pride in 2013 (second African country to host one); 82% public acceptance of a 'homosexual' neighbour (2019-2021 polls); LGBTIQ organisations can register; no same-sex union recognition; committed at its 2024 UPR to improve protections; only African UN LGBTI Core Group member besides South Africa.

sources.title: Cape Verde: The LGBTI Pride week in Praia, Cabo Verde — Equal Eyes
sources.claim_summary: Equal Eyes (July 2018): Cape Verde's LGBTI Pride week in Praia - supported by the government's Institute for Gender Equality (ICIEG), Spanish Cooperation and City Hall; Pride began in Mindelo in 2013; activists campaign for same-sex marriage and an anti-LGBTIphobia non-discrimination law; slogan 'De boa com quem sou'.
NOTE: This is the State Department's archived reports index page (navigation only); the specific Cabo Verde report content was not retrievable.

sources.title: Casamento gay não está na agenda cabo-verdiana – Observador
sources.claim_summary: Observador/Lusa (July 2017, in Portuguese): Cape Verde's PM said same-sex marriage is not on the government's political agenda, calling it 'opinion' - responding to LGBT community claims to union and marriage rights.

Afrobarometer Dispatch No. 362 (May 2020): 'All in this together' - Africans are tolerant on ethnic, religious and national differences but not sexual differences; Cabo Verde, Namibia and São Tomé and Príncipe stand out as particularly tolerant countries; tolerance toward sexual minorities remains remarkably weak even among younger respondents.

sources.title: Tchinda Andrade - Rede Angola - Notícias independentes sobre Angola
sources.claim_summary: Rede Angola special (June 2016, in Portuguese): interview with Tchinda Andrade, the first person to come out publicly as trans in Cape Verde (1997, during Mindelo Carnival) - describes Cape Verde as 'a country with freedom relative to the LGBT mass', Mindelo as relaxed, though she experienced verbal violence and two physical attacks (possibly robbery-motivated).
